recs.name: Breeze's Warmth, Chilled Forest
recs.tag: To shed a noble identity does not entail running away.

lines.st: Eulogy—
I've been going with this two-hundred-odd Leithanian refugee group for...
I can't even tell how many days it's been.
At Leithanien's border region, Catastrophe brought about an earthquake, which in turn caused the river to breach its levee.
These poor people lost their home, sought shelter somewhere higher on instinct, and fled all the way here.
The winter days are looming, and many are ill. We're stuck in place.
We have only temporary shelters cobbled together with wood, open to the elements, until help comes for us.
We're currently in Victoria's northwest, near the mountains of Kjerag, far removed from any cities.
As cold weather approaches, our food is running bare. No clothing that can keep us warm, and all medicine has been used up.
Eulogy... this operation turned out nothing like I thought. How could it be so arduous, so tough... Where are the humanitarians, the philanthropic barons...
Dad...
We're still trying, but... so many of us are slowly dying... I'm stood in all this passing away, and I can't see the light.

lines.x: Victorian northwest border region, somewhere in the forests
(I can't shake this feeling someone's been tailing me the whole time.)
(Heheh, don't look away now!)
Ah! These are the footprints of—!
An omnivorous beast! The teeth are in fairly shabby shape. But its claws are sharp; chances are, it tears its prey to slivers before it eats.
It shouldn't ordinarily attack people, but supposing food runs low in winter... they might just start picking off human stragglers...
Aaaah!
Ah, wh-whah, wha-wha-aaaaaah—!
Grace—!!!
Buh, bah, whaaaah, don't leave me all alone!!!
So it was you, Rita. Get over here, quickly.
Grace, Grace!! There was rustling in those bushes over there!! It's a beast! Is this where we're going to die?
Hahaha! Don't lose your head, I made all that up on the spot.
I was just curious who was creeping around behind me, and here you are.
Mmph!
Come on, Grace, don't scare me like that!
Well, I might've made up the beasts, but people who secretly follow you are plenty dangerous too.
Now, confess. Why are you tracking me?
I—I was hungry.
You were hungry, so you followed me looking for food? I don't know, you seem pretty chipper to me, don't you?
Mama and Papa don't have anything to eat. They gave their last bit of food to me...
How about the harvest group's food?
Mama got ill forever ago. After Papa got hurt hunting, the harvest group all said our family doesn't work for anything, and they don't want to give us food...
And they said, it's winter now, and they can barely find any food like this. There's not enough stores in camp, and unless it gets warmer, we'll be more and more short on food.
(That's true enough. The situation's continued to deteriorate.)
(If help still doesn't show up, then when the time comes...)
And... even if I went with them, I don't have any contribution to make to the hunt. They just won't share anything with me. So the last few days, I haven't gone with them...
Is that how they're going to be now?!
*whimper*... Both Mama and Papa are sleeping on sickbeds, and it's cold, and I can't eat enough to not be hungry. I don't feel good.
Grace, can you help tell me which things are edible? I want to pick some stuff before I go back...
Even just some weeds would be okay. It doesn't matter how bad it tastes, either. As long as I can feel fuller, it's fine!
No problem, leave it to me! But just eating weeds you find on the wayside won't do it. If you really want to be full, you'll want beast meat too.
The food you ultimately get from scrabbling around here won't be enough in the long-term, versus the effort you spend.
But I—I can't catch beasts.
Mmm... leave that for today, then. Emergencies first. Tomorrow, I'll take you up north, and we'll see if we can't catch a few little beasties for ourselves!
Really? Thank you, Grace!
This is great! Mama and Papa can eat properly too!
Save your thanks just for now. In exchange, listen to what I say today, and don't go scarpering off, got it?
Got it!
Oh, careful where you're stepping! Don't you trip over.
Hehe...
Are we looking for herbs we can eat now? Mama and Papa are waiting for me to bring back food!
Ah, this one looks like a herb! Grace, is this one edible?
Hm... it might look very much like you could eat it, but it's actually poisonous.
Um, then what about this one here?
Not that one either. It's too tough to chew, and you'll make your mouth bleed.
Then this one! It's a fruit! It's fresh, too. Is this one okay?
This is a cysteye. A berry that looks just like a cystybeast's eye, right?
But it's not edible. It looks plenty delicious, and it's sweet if you try it too. But, afterwards, it'll give you tremendous tummy problems, and the more you eat, the worse it'll get.

Some Victorian nobles use them as weight-loss drugs, run themselves dry eating them, then their lowered immunity leads to all sorts of illness... no matter if it fills you, it's awful for the human body.
Giving other species the runs to spread its own seeds. Evolution truly goes in funny ways, sometimes.
*whimper*—What do we do then?! We can't find anything to eat at all.
Don't lose heart. The fruit might not be edible, but you can eat its leaves. They're a little bitter, but won't do any damage to the body. Boiling them will help take some of the edge off.
Then I'll pick just a few leaves to try.
Heheh, I'll say your luck's not too bad! Look at what I'm holding—you can go find a few of these too.
Are those pebbles?
Look on top of them. These are wild mossoats—these spores here look just like oats, that's why. You can eat these.
The books said some of Ursus's farming peasantry in the Northern Tundra grow these, but I never imagined we'd find some here too.
That's superb! I'll go pick some too!
The more, the better. Pull off the husks, wash them, and you can boil them for a thin porridge.
But if we pick them all now, won't there be no more left later?

The mossoat harvest cycle goes by in a flash. After the harvest period, its sugar content gets absorbed, the spores on top are formed, the 'oat' part of it withers some, and it turns bitter and inedible.
Then are these ones right now good mossoats?
They are! You've got sound luck, Rita! But these are wild ones after all—they won't be plenty. You'll want to pick all of these to have enough for a full pot.
I'll go for it, then!
Incredible stuff, Rita. I'll help you out too.
Thank you, Grace! Hehe, I'm gonna pick loads, and then I'll hide them all, and only give them to Mama and Papa!
Once I pick all the mossoats, I'll come pick the medicine herbs with you, Grace!
Perfect. You look around this flat area, then, and don't go too far. I'll see what's westwards. If anything happens, just shout for me!
Mm-hm! I got it, Grace!
(It's raining...)
(Brrr. The stones are starting to get slippery, too.)
(About time I go back and check on Rita.)
Ritaaaaa—!!
Iiii'm—oooo—veeer—heeeere—
(Why is she so far away?)
Rita?? Where are you??
Iiii'm—dooown—heeeere—
Huh?!
Iiiii—wasn't—caaareful—and—Iiiii—sliiipped—dooown—heeeree—
Are you hurt?!
Don't move about! I'll be down in a flash!
Graaace—beeee—caaaare—
Aaaaagh—!
Ah! I wanted to tell you it was really slippery over there, so careful not to step on the stones and fall down here too.
What does this pit think it is, a slide?!
Hahaha, there's grass growing from your head now!
Oh? How about you join in with me? Hupsie-daisy!
Aha! A moustache!
Achoo! Ah—ah—achoo! *whimper*... You got all the leafy stuff stuck in my nose, Grace. It's itchy.
Pff! Watch your snot—you've got snot coming out!
Nnn...
Hahahahahahahahahahaha!!
Alright, I'm done picking on you. Anyhow, what have you been doing down here?
I couldn't find more mossoats up above, so I went to see if there were any underground, so I could pick even more.
And then I wasn't careful and I fell!
Are you hurt?
I landed on my butt a little hard, but everything else is okay.
Phew. Thank goodness for that.
Weren't you supposed to be listening to me? I never told you to come anywhere like this, did I?
But I only have enough for one pot, and it's not that much. Besides, if we went harvesting tomorrow and it was too late, wouldn't they all be wasted?
You still have to mind your own safety, though.
Mm-hm... I left my basket up above, so it's alright!
I saw it just now. Which is why I left my basket there too.
Next to mine?
Yep, all snuggly.
Hehehe, that's really nice.
It's raining now. Here, put this on you. Don't catch a cold now.
This leaf is huge!
I picked it just before. Wear it on your head, put your horns through these two holes, and that'll block the rain.
My ears are chilly. I feel a little bad.
Don't you take it off. The rain'll love to give you a cold if it soaks you. If you get ill too, who's going to care for your mum and dad?
That's right, I'm our provider now! I have to make sure Mama and Papa are well-fed!
Hmm?
Grace, aren't you gonna put on a leaf?
You wear yours for now.
I've actually barely ever gotten rain-soaked. Feels a little unlike anything else.
How come—how come you never got wet in the rain before?
Maybe Victoria doesn't get that much rain, actually?
Rain's a very common sight in Victoria, to be clear, but it's true—I've never been able to shower in it.
Especially like now. Nothing between me and the final rains of autumn, pattering on my head...
Then I'm even stronger than you are! When it's raining, I fetch laundry outside all the time, and do farm work.
Rain is pretty much like when the village headman got mad at me. He went, Rita, pbphth, whatbth is phthe meaning of thisph thbphruckus—!
Hahahaha! Oh, that headman. Just like a spit sprinkler when worked up.
But he can't sprinkle anymore now...
He'd just gotten too old. Too tired, too.
I saw it. That day I secretly followed you, and saw you carrying him out on your back, and you were really struggling to take him so far away, and then soon after you put him down, he just...
Just floated away like ash, like when we burn wood...
Will my Mama and Papa become like that too?
It's been two weeks already since the distress team left. Given they're following my map, they should've found a nearby town by now.
Besides, I've picked so much medicine today, and you've picked plenty of food too. Your mum and dad will be just fine!
Right! I've worked really hard! Mama and Papa are gonna be better for sure!
By the way, Grace, why don't you let anyone else help you pick medicine?
Mm... you know, everyone's in the same boat as your family. They can't eat their fill now, so securing food is more or less top priority for them all.
That's why nobody has a hand to lend, see.
The rain's getting stronger, it looks like. Your mum and dad will be worried about you. Head on back first, okay? I can find the rest of the herbs we need by myself.
Mm-hm! I need to bring back everything I picked. I bet Mama and Papa are just as hungry.
Can you still tell the way back?
Of course I can!
Then I'll lift you up out of here. Careful, now.
Hnph!
I'm out!
Grace, grab my hand now, I'll pull you up!
Hahaha, I'm miles heavier than you are! I can climb out by myself! Don't worry about me, hurry back and check in on your mum and dad!
Alright~
Don't run too fast! Watch your step!
Alriiight—
Hm... and now we worry about what I'm doing.
I just saw the herbs I needed on the cliff over there.
The rain's not going to make this tunnel hard for me, but am I still going to make it up that cliff?
Yowch, I must've gashed that ankle when I fell down. The wound's fairly big. Need something to stop the bleeding first.
But I'm not going to win at any gymnastics once I'm bound up. That makes the cliff even harder.
*hiss*! God, my ankle hurts... I'm feeling a little dizzy too. Have I gotten fatigued lately?
Rita's mum's in terrible shape. Her dad's suffered external wounds, and I gave first-aid treatment, but it's still at risk of infection.
The nobles couldn't have possibly missed refugees entering their estate, so why are they so unconcerned... not even just to deport them... why haven't they shown up?
The refugees long since ran out of pharmaceuticals, and now all they have is plant remedies for simple treatment. I need to pick more. I need to be able to help more!
I hope to heaven we can last until the distress team comes back with someone. I hope to heaven...
Ah, I can't get bogged down in this. If I let the rain get any worse, that cliff'll only be harder! I need to hurry and pick what I need! I'll bandage myself after I'm back down!
Victorian northwest border region, refugee camp
Fever medicine for the Hanses. This much should do the trick...
Toothache painkillers for Peter, but the pain is all it kills... these few herbals might not be quite enough.
Bug repellant... ugh, why am I missing something! Hunger must've shook it out of my mind. I'll go back outside to search later... it's already dark now, and the rain's not dying down...
Huh? Why's someone at the entrance to my room?
Miss Arizona!
Miss Arizona!!!!
I'm coming! I'm right here!
Miss Arizona, where on Terra were you?! Some—Someone's gotten extremely sick, out of nowhere!
What?!
(It can't be another case like the village headman, can it?)
Where? Show me to them!
Here. Right in here.
This room is...?
Rita's family's?!
Rita? Are you doing alright?
No reaction... palms severely scalded, contusions on arms, swelling on the back of the head. Nnn... and a slight fever. She was so well before, too.
When did you find her like this?
Just now, about twenty minutes ago.
What did you come to Rita's for?
Uh...
Her parents are in the treatment area. It was her all alone here, making dinner for her mother and father. What were you doing here?
I... I... She didn't come picking with us today, that's why! So I just came to see if something was wrong!
Liar! She said the harvest group wouldn't share anything with her! She hasn't gone with them for several days now!
If you truly cared about that, you would've come much earlier, not just now!
Where's the food she picked today? Why isn't it in this room? Did you break in here and steal her food?
I'm just trying to help my family survive too! There's not much food anywhere left at all!
I didn't know... she'd resist so hard... I didn't know... and now she's in this state...
Victoria's nobles will not overlook us. The distress team we sent should have found a city by now!
And even if that's true, my children won't be able to last until then.
That doesn't call for robbing a young girl of her food! She collected it by her own efforts.
This scalding on her palms was because out of fear of you stealing it, she directly tried to carry the boiling pot away, right?
The contusions on her arms were from you grabbing her, right?
The back of her head was you pushing her and knocking her against something, RIGHT?
I didn't... mean to hurt her like this...
Her mother and father are done for! Even if she survives, so what? Before long, she'll just be a... an orphan! Even if everything gets better, she can't live on alone!
My children and I are still healthy! Surely our whole family surviving carries more weight than her.
Is that it? You'll weigh their lives...?
Then how about me? My life? How much weight do you see in me?
I've had a little hunch you've all been gawping at me and my Eulogy, whispering about who in the world I could be.
So be so kind as to tell me, how much weight do you see in this single life of mine?
M—Madam! You've treated us, saved us, some of us have guessed you might be a Victorian noble... out of all of us here, you're the most honorable...
Then shouldn't you be giving your food to me, making my survival easier?
Because I—for one—haven't eaten well in a very long time!
...That's...
But you wouldn't be willing to give food to me, would you?
You don't follow any logic, or reason, or any just course of action. All you are is selfish.
I—despise—the selfish, and I'd let alone even the thought of aiding a robber.
In light of you at the VERY least informing me about this, I'll give you one more chance—
Return the food, with not one bit missing! If you've eaten it, make up for it! Or else I guarantee, the distress group's caravan will have no place for you in it.
Yes... I understand, madam.
*sigh*. So I have it in my nature to tell petrifying lies like that too. Whatever, as long as it had a use.
Rita...
Malnutrition, fever, physical trauma, inflammation.
I'll give this fever medication to Rita for now, seeing as it's prepared. If I don't have enough, I can pick some more in a bit to give to the patients in the treatment area.
*whimper*... don't steal my Mama and Papa's porridge...!
Rita! It's me, Grace. I'm just borrowing your pot for the moment, decocting some herbs for you. No need to be scared.
Take this drink in a moment, and you'll feel a little better.
My Mama and Papa's... food... got... stolen...
It's okay, your food will come back. Just trust in me for now, and get some rest.
Mnn...
Here, I've already blown it cool it for you, Rita. Open your mouth a bit.
That's great, Rita! There's a little spilling from your mouth. Let me wipe that for you.
It'll be effective soon. Just sleep here for a bit. I'll go fetch some other medicines for you!
Zzz... zzz...
Already asleep? That's some effective medicine. Just wait for me, now, I'll be right back.
It's pouring buckets now... so dark...
I need to move quick! If I'm any later, I won't be able to see it!
My foot... ow...
I remember the herbs I was looking for were right near here... leaves like arrowheads, fine sawteeth on top. Ah! Is this it?
There! All clean. Now to grind into a powder!
Hmm...
Why do I start swooning the moment I apply any force...
Come on, please, just hold on a little more!
Okay, and these herbals in matching proportion.
Ah, there's not enough firewood!
Temperature... I need to collect more firewood.
Ohh...
Rita. Rita. Don't be scared. I'll feed you some medicine now. It might be a tiny bit... hot.
Oh, I think I forgot to pick out the seeds... it might be very bitter, too.
I've already applied topical medication to you. This is for reducing your fever. Here, drink, and you'll be much better soon.
I won't let anything happen to you...
(Strained gulp)
Heehee, good girl, Rita!
So dizzy... I can't keep... should—I rest for a moment...?
Rita...
Rita... Rita... you have to...
She was like this when we found her, mumbling the name over and over.
She's covered in mud, her ankle is injured, and she has minor Oripathy infection symptoms. Was she only recently infected?
Oripathy infection is only one part of it. The major contributing factors to her fainting were starvation and extreme exhaustion.
Reports say she's been passed out for several days now. Some refugees say this young woman was protecting them. Without her efforts, hardly this many would have survived.

The refugees regained capacity for labor after recovering, and were able to request treatment and a place to stay from Mr. Gurk of Leithanien. He required people to staff and safeguard that bizarre castle of his.

These people's home was struck by severe Catastrophe. Going back seems unlikely at present, so most refugees have accepted this proposal. They're prepared to undergo treatment at Mr. Gurk's, and to wait for now to see if they should return home.
Only the reasonable grounds of allowing these refugees to return to their home country could convince any related nobles not to interfere.
About the young girl named Rita. Her mother has already passed on. Fortunately, her handicapped father is still able to work.

A Catastrophe Messenger in the vicinity mentioned Earthspirit on the Rhodes Island landship is an old acquaintance of Gurk's. I'll write her a letter asking for a favor, to see if this father and daughter can be admitted onto his estate.

The young Vulpo lady was unorthodox enough to leave deep impressions on people, but plucking herbal medicine and understanding some clinical theory was all she had. No way of suppressing her own Oripathy.
She's too simple about the task of aiding refugees. It would've cost her her life sooner or later if she was too reductive about it.
In a moment, I want you to make contact with a nearby Messenger. There's two letters I want to send. One to Rhodes Island, and another to a place in Toron.

I'm compelled to remind you, Victoria has nobles who want those refugees dead here to serve their vie over territory. So as to keep our motive secure, we cannot at this moment openly represent Rhodes Island.

lines.st: ...Rhodes Island?

lines.x: Not to mention you slipped out of a Victorian medical seminar to come here. Your actions must be kept subdued. It'll be best you don't give even more issues the chance to form.
Oh, I was in an academic seminar, huh. See, these past few days, I was under the impression I'd be participating in some wannabe Durins' wine-tasting.
Heh. To some nobles, philanthropy is a trend, and a trend is as far as it goes. They weighed the pros and cons, and did something anyone could've seen coming from a mile off.
She's too weak. If we don't immediately treat her, further illness will seize hold of her, and we'll see her Oripathy infection accelerate.
Let her pass off as my assistant and get the best treatment Victoria has to offer.
Yeah, no kidding, we're gonna keep our true identities a secret from her. You happy with that?
Assistant? Why do I suspect you're thinking of having her by your side?
I'm no nanny. You ever seen me drop in from the Victorian skies on an umbrella?
Once she recovers, I'll contact a specialist place and get her on a course for medical Arts, and I've got other fish to fry in the meanwhile.
If she wants to keep up her innocent little savior business, I'm not gonna write in to complain.

But as a doctor with Oripathy, she's got no choice. She can't keep playing the wild maverick forever. Bottom line, she needs to learn how to protect herself. How her own future spirals out is her business.
Suit yourself. *sigh*. I suppose once Scout's done with his mission, I'll be transferring to his squad anyway. Having a Victorian local by your side to keep an eye on you works out.
I weep for that Vulpo...
She's sure as hell a lot more confident than you when she treats people.
Hm. And her prescriptions when treating non-Oripathy patients are particularly effective.
I think I see what it is.
Kindness, strength, honesty, a tender age yet already at such standards.
You want to defend a possibility.
Yes, I'd... very much like to see how she does too. It's a shame I'll probably be on my way back to Rhodes Island before she wakes up.

lines.st: Rhodes Island...?

lines.x: Brave young Vulpo, do get better soon.
There's still so many people waiting for you—I'll be waiting too, to see how you grow, what you become.
But I suppose you probably can't hear me right now... hahah...
I want to witness your future too, young Vulpo.
If we've been brought together, if we'll ever meet again in future, maybe at Rhodes Island, maybe in some other place somewhere...

lines.st: Rhodes... Island...
Eulogy—
After coming aboard Rhodes Island, I never could find that warm voice again.
Lady Earthspirit and Mr. Gurk continued correspondence. Rita is currently... not doing well, per se, but at least she can eat her fill.
And I'm doing... very busily here at Rhodes Island. It's very fulfilling, too. I've been in the company of truly outstanding doctors and scholars, trying some major things without break.
Eulogy... thank you all, for forgiving the scene I made.
I'm sorry. I've...
Caught Oripathy.
I'm stood on this vast world, Oripathy stretching far and wide—
And I hope... there'll come a day of finality, from where I can see the light.

recs.name: Prisoner's Dream
recs.tag: They are dissatisﬁed with their present, and devote their lives to another path, but in the end, there was no path leading to happiness. The cycle repeats, time runs out, and only sorrow remains.

lines.x: Arizona Manor, North Rockbrook, County of Toron
Ahem...
Letter for you, Miss Grace.
Miss Grace is changing.
She's been sneaking out almost every day while her parents are away. Shouldn't we do something?
Well, you could start by chopping down the tree outside the window. If you expect me to do something about it through her clothes though, I assure you I've tried everything.
I haven't seen you try anything.
Perhaps you should see an eye doctor then, Mr. Counsell.
Letter for you, Miss Grace.
Leave it on the table.
Aren't you going to read it?
No need. I can more or less guess what it's about.
The typical greeting, then asking after my parents, then regretfully declining my request with some excuse or other...
The young Vulpo sits before the dresser, dolefully fidgeting with the receiver in her hands, the indicator light on it flashing red.
She would have been overjoyed if it had flashed yesterday, or the day before.
*sigh*...
Maybe I shouldn't be wasting my time writing these letters or reading the responses.
When will Father and Mother return? I should be ready to greet them.
Oh, I'm terribly sorry! We were so busy downstairs that I forgot to tell you.
His Lordship sent word that he and Her Ladyship have been invited to a bookstore's opening ceremony. A well-compensated appearance, I'm told.
He would have been better off using his pen name. No doubt it's worth even more than the title of Baron Arizona.
Well, he used to write some awfully cynical things under that name, so he stopped using it once he became The Right Honourable Henry Arizona.
Better safe than sorry, after all. Who knows how many nobles were involved in what he criticized?
So he gets to choose his identity, while I'm forced to accept the life he decided for me.
Wait, so how long is this delay?
A day.
If I didn't know any better, I'd think that grin meant you were planning to sneak out again.
Sorry, I just remembered something urgent!
Miss Grace!
Temporary accommodation site, Rockbrook outskirts, County of Toron
Near the forests, where civilization meets wilderness, a group of despondent people have been abandoned.
The wet morning mist fades away, and the sun's rays shine into the dark grey forest.
Guys, I'm back!
You again? What is it this time? Like this place isn't messy enough already.
Do you remember the health information I asked you for last time?
Right, four days ago. Haven't seen your face since.
Well, I couldn't get back to you because—
Because we couldn't hold up our end of the deal? You wanted information on Marianne, and you thought we were hiding something, so you left us hanging to see if we'd loosen our tongues.
Settle down, friend. She's not your foreman, she's just a little girl. Why would she be playing tricks like that?
Don't judge a book by its cover. Who knows what lies beneath the surface?
You do owe us an explanation though, young Vulpo. Why did you need our health information?
Like I said, I asked many doctors, and only one didn't reject me out of hand.
He said if I got your personal information—to learn more about your health—then he could come and help.
Unfortunately, he was out when I brought him the data, and hasn't been back to his office in a few days...
What a coincidence!
Let her finish.
...So all I could do was wait, and keep searching for another way.
I did place a transmitter on the door to his clinic though, so I'll get a signal when he opens it! Look, this red light has been blinking since morning.
What are you doing here then? Shouldn't you be off looking for him?
I wanted to get updated information, since I'm not sure if the reports from four days ago are still recent enough... I don't know much about this, I just thought it would be safer this way.
Pull the other one. You only wanted news about Marianne, you never really cared about us. Why should we trust you?
I—
You don't need to answer him. He's still under the delusion that the nobles will come and help us.
Phooey! Of course they will! They just don't know about our situation yet.
Marianne's been missing for quite some time. No matter how much effort you devote to helping us, we can hardly conjure her out of thin air.
I know that. I'm not too worried about her. It's more important to focus on the here and now.
She's a child, same age as you. Who knows what could happen in the forest?
I knew her before I moved here, and we used to sneak out and play together. She loves plants, and there are enough in there to keep her from going hungry at least.
Her first letter asked me to take care of you, and I'd rather she not nag me when she gets back, so...
Well, no matter what anyone else says, I'm on your side. I'll help you persuade them too, if it comes to it.
Thank you.
Why don't you start your info gathering with me then? I need to go cut some wood once we're done here.
What for?
We want to build a bigger house, to fit everyone. Things will get better.
Yes, they will.
Siew Clinic, Rockbrook, County of Toron
An old office lies near the town walls. Grace was last here four days ago, and the dust in the corner has only grown thicker since then.
The windows are covered in grime. They once faced the entire town; now, the melody of industry converges on the west ones only.
A small man sits before the table, muttering in some foreign tongue peppered with a few Victorian words.

The bill...
The bill...
The bloody bill!
Ahem—
We're booked for today.
I got what you asked for.
The doctor looks up with a start. The frames of east windows cast long, trapezoidal shadows.
A Vulpo stands at his door, her golden hair glittering in the sun.
Here. I've organized them.
...You really did it.
How did you compile these reports? You're just a child.
I have some medical books at home. I like to flip through them whenever I get grounded.
Just for reference, though. I'm sure there are still plenty of mistakes.
Well done... Well done indeed...
Your turn.
About that...
I have to visit the Pelham Manor today. Can we talk about this after I get back?
The name Pelham strikes Grace like a bolt of lightning.
An ominous sign.
Why?
My patients do expect me to visit them.
I meant, why do I have wait until after you visit her?
So... this really is about her?
You're not her private doctor. She lives in the nomadic city, only visiting here once a month to supervise the factory. Why does everyone do as she says?
It's not that simple.
You're under her thumb. Just like everyone else.
She doesn't control me.
But things are an awful lot easier with her support, aren't they?
Listen, girl.
To them, I'm a luxury, something fashionable, a lifestyle, value added. That's the foundation on which my life and my family are built. I can't turn my back on it now.
My rent, my child's tuition, my wife's Oripathy treatment... I can't afford to lose this job.
This isn't one of those fairy tales where you can defeat the evil and everybody lives happily ever after. The true enemy is formless. It's a byproduct of living. It's life itself.
And how is helping these poor people at odds with a noble's interests?
I'm not Her Ladyship. I can't see the full picture.
They're just ordinary, harmless people you'd find anywhere.
And if they're really so unimportant, do you think they'd be treated this way?
As for other nobles, I doubt any of them would risk getting on the wrong side of the daughter of a newspaper mogul who married into the Pelham family and owns a number of factories.
I'm almost out of free time, Dr. Siew. It was only by happy accident that I could make it today. I wanted to make the most of this spot of luck, along with the hope you gave me.
If I haven't done enough, then tell me, and I'll keep trying.
And what exactly have you done?
I asked many people for help.
So you're placing all your hopes on others.
I suppose you're right...
I'm in no position to criticize you. However—
I envy you. You have both talent and innocence. Your motives are simple. You're young, energetic, passionate. Life hasn't yet pulled the trigger on you.
But why not do it yourself? What are you so worried about?
My family may not approve. Or the Pelhams. Or the people of the town...
Hold on, back up. You're just a child. You shouldn't feel bound by such matters. Don't think about it like that.
Listen...
The night I made my promise to you, I wrote to her and mentioned it. She hinted that luxury is a complicated thing, taking its value from many sources.
For example, it would be worthless if it were given away to the poor for free.
She implored me not to lose sight of my 'consumers.'
She threatened you.
It wasn't a threat. She didn't need to. It was a reminder. Even if were to become a right bastard, it wouldn't affect her one way or another.
...Although I suppose I already am.
I gave you false hope, and now I have to be blunt...
I'm sorry, but I only made that promise because I didn't think a child like you would really try to help them.
So you wanted to refuse from the beginning, but couldn't say it to my face?
I'm sorry I got your hopes up.
Do you know the Arizona family? I'm... friends with their daughter. Would you agree to help if she asked you directly?
If you're friends with a noble, that's all the more reason not to view them so simply.
The Arizonas have no stake in this, so they have no reason to butt heads with the Pelhams.
But those people are dying. Shouldn't they care? What about honor?
Nobles are nobles because they're recognized as such. But they don't need the recognition of commoners, just other nobles.
Honor is simply an accessory adorning their power and wealth.
But what if the Arizonas aren't like other nobles? I'm really close to their daughter, I know they're different!
Face it, they're all the same.
Did you think Lady Arizona and the baron were really in love?
Their marriage was based on mutual interest, as most of theirs are. One side gained social status, the other gained powerful Originium Arts.
I don't think they're any different from other nobles. If anything, they're still struggling to find their footing, making them all the more conservative.
Are you saying my—
Are you saying the baron and baroness are...
She could not go on. Logic and syntax break apart, along with something deep inside her heart.
Like the snow castles that Counsell built for her, helplessly waiting for the changing of seasons.
Melted snow fills her eyes.
It's getting late. I have to hurry to Pelham Manor, then go into town to deal with the mess my son caused at school.
I'll write if anything comes up.
I apologize. You're young... but you're honorable.
I... I'll find someone else.
I'm sorry.
Town Park, Rockbrook, County of Toron
*sigh*...
Ladies and gentleman, I say again, I found this man cutting down our trees!
He is destroying our property!
Today they cut our trees, tomorrow they'll take our food, then our jobs, then our land!
Defend our property! Defend our jobs! Defend our town!
Defend our property! Defend our jobs! Defend our town!
What are you doing?!
No, Miss Grace!
Counsell? What are you doing here?
That man has ties to the Pelham family. He'll recognize you.
But I know the man they have tied up! I have to help him!
Let me go!
Miss Grace... there are people here who know you. That makes you a daughter of the Arizonas, and your every word and deed that of your family's.
Your status does not permit you to interfere.
What if I say I don't care?
Your servants at home do. They have livelihoods and families. They need steady jobs.
Look at these people. They've never cared about the trees before.
Lady Pelham is most shrewd. She's made the townsfolk despise these people from the bottom of their hearts. Made her will theirs.
Step forward now, and you put Arizona at odds with the entire town.
This is a complicated matter. If you truly want to intervene, you had best wait for His Lordship to return. They won't keep him tied up for long; it's risky, even for them.
Please, calm down. I must answer to your father.
I understand.
Your aunt did not know that your parents were going to be late. She's already on her way here, and we will be welcoming her as planned.
We couldn't very well turn her away... All the servants have their hands full. We had no choice but to simplify the menu and courses.
And since we have a guest, we require a hostess. I came to bring you back.
...Apparently, Miss Grace Arizona has more important matters to attend to.
Please come with me. The manor needs you.
But...

lines.st: His head is bowed, but Grace could feel his piercing gaze, like a sword running her through.
A sorrow far too deep for a girl her age spreads inside her.

lines.x: Arizona Manor, North Rockbrook, County of Toron
Not this one... This one's no good either...
This one...
Why not the previous one?
You've been so busy lately that your skin has lost some sheen. I need to find something that can make it shine.
Our guest will be arriving in but a few minutes. We should be at the entrance to greet her.
Don't rush me, Mr. Counsell!
Here, this one!
'Miss Grace' does not respond. She leans back in her chair, gazing out the window, while the servants line up to greet the guest.
She casts her gaze towards the town factory as it energetically churns out black smoke in the distance.
It is quiet.
Neither summer nor winter have come as promised.
Her gaze returns to the dresser. The letter that came that morning still lies there.
I mended this dress just this afternoon. Look at the sequins I sewed on!
Are you finally reading the letter? I'll fetch a letter opener.
No need. I already have it open...
Mr. Counsell! Stop Miss Grace!
Huh?
*Pant* I-I'm out of breath... *pant* hurry...
Have the new manservant clean this up.
Out of my way!
The banquet is about to start, Miss Grace. As a servant of the Arizonas, I can't let you run around like this.
What is this about?
I said out of my way!
What happened? I can't decide whether to obey unless you tell me.
A Messenger went into the forest and found some...
There was a girl was carrying a pile of letters. Nothing written on them, except the sender and recipient. I'm the recipient, and the sender was...
Marianne... it was two weeks ago.
...My condolences, Miss Grace.
It's all my fault.
I assure you it is not. I witnessed your efforts with my very own eyes.
Did you now? And what precisely have I done?
From the very beginning, I knew nothing of what they were dealing with.
I could empathize with their suffering, but only on the surface. I just assumed someone would help them, that it would get better.
For the past few months, all I've done is play the role of the young lady of the house, while writing a few letters in my spare time. None of which amounted to anything.
But when I finally met them directly these past few days, I realized that what I had empathized with was less than a fraction of their real pain and suffering.
They need help, Counsell. They shouldn't end up like Marianne.
It's not your place to do so. You're the daughter of the Arizonas.
This isn't the place to stand on status. We're all equal before such suffering.
Do the baron and baroness know of this?
No. I was afraid they would be angry, and make it even harder to do anything.
Perhaps you could tell them once they return.
I heard something about Father and Mother today.
I don't think they're any different from the people I wrote to, seeking help...
Love and kindness are mere illusions when it comes to nobles... even Dr. Siew lied to me.
But at least he suggested to go among them and check up on their health, to give them some basic advice about medicine.
I even noticed that some of them had gotten better when I visited them today.
That sort of thing is what's really worth doing... to me, at least.
Why should I wait for others to act? I can't entrust these people's lives and hopes to others. I can't keep fooling myself and putting things off.
Miss Grace, we should wait for your parents to—
How long am I supposed to wait?!
My friend is dead! While she was struggling on the brink of death, I was busy socializing, busy watching my words, busy managing Arizona's relationships with other nobles!
Do I have to stay at home, asking for help in proper, dignified, useless ways, while I watch those who trusted in me get lynched?
Is nobility meant to be a shackle, Counsell?
Maintaining proper etiquette in your social life is all for the sake of the Arizona family's honor and reputation. If it can regain its former glory, it can shine its light on yet more people.
They don't have the time. Neither do I.
They were forced to wander because they lost their land. And they'll die slowly while I enjoy the comfort of high society, just as Marianne did...
What's the point of it all, if the favor of these nobles has to be earned at every turn? If I can bring them back to health, they'll light their own torch, find their own way in the darkness.
Miss Grace...
I'm sorry, Counsell. I'm not angry at you.
I just needed to vent, like how some people turn to drinking or hunting.
I need to do something. I can't live like this without changing.
Let me do something useful, in what few days I have.
Very well, then. You should start by reading these then.
These are...
From the manor library. You remember them, don't you? The baron's translation, which you've flipped through so many times.
There will always be little details that slip your mind, of course. Bring them along for reference.
Counsell...
I've seen this play before. I can't stop you.
I'll tell them I couldn't catch you. Just don't let it slip that I let you go on purpose.
...Thank you.
Hold on, Miss Grace.
You're not going back on your words, are you?
I visited Dr. Siew to retrieve the trinket you 'forgot' on his door.

He told me that if I ever saw the young lady's Vulpo 'friend,' I should tell her that he most definitely did not forget to close the clinic's window, and certainly did not leave various medicines and supplies on the table.
I see...
There will be no hiding your little sojourn. Have you thought about what you'll do when your father returns? I doubt arguing will help the matter.
I'll apologize. I'm not ready to argue with him yet.
Be careful, and keep your identity a secret.
Thank you, Counsell.
Is Miss Grace still in the library?
Yes. It's like she's a whole different person.
I only regret that I might have cost you your job.
My job? Miss Grace has been spending her days in the library rather than sneaking out. Why would I lose my job?
A single meaningful journey is worth a thousand frivolous trips. She's not the little girl she once was.
Thank goodness for that.
Aren't you concerned?
If that's her choice, then her light shouldn't belong to me alone.
You...
Her light, is it?
Counsell gazes to the west and sees the light of the setting sun fall on the floor of the Arizona Manor.
Old memories rise to the surface.
She's your daughter alright, Henry.
